newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Electra lowered to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Electra lowered to hold.

text.p: Israel's Sahar Securities and Investments lowered its rating for Electra Israel Ltd to a hold from a buy in a report released on Sunday.

Analyst Boaz Levitan said the downgrading was due to a high price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and the industry cycle, which he said indicated that earnings had peaked for the maker of building electromechanical systems.
Levitan noted that the growth in non-residential construction investment had fallen sharply since 1993 and more recently had begun to contract.
"It is evident that this cycle is ebbing and is bound to have an impact upon the company's growth rate," he said, noting that Electra's orders backlog had barely grown during the first quarter.

Levitan added, however, that he did not expect the downturn in construction to last long, citing Israel's underdeveloped tourism, transport and business infrastructure. "This shortage is bound to return the company to a track of growth in 1999," he said.
He said Electra's P/E, at 14.8 times 1997 earnings based on a share price of 167.7 shekels, was high given that earnings had likely peaked. Electra shares closed last Thursday at 157.23 shekels.
Sahar put a target price for Electra of 170 to 180 shekels for the coming year.
